clue.text: Nothing accomplished, sweetheart

parts.note: love is zero, nil, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A lament that nothing has been achieved, addressed to a darling.
explanation.definitionFit: A loved one is a beloved partner or darling, the person one holds dearest.

clue.text: Clear mobility handicap I had contracted

parts.note: a limp is an uneven walk caused by injury
I had shortened with an apostrophe becomes I'd

explanation.surface: Someone recalls catching an illness that left them lame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' looks like catching a disease but means shortened, as I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid water is perfectly transparent, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Delivery truck lad turns hoodlum

parts.note: a van is a vehicle for deliveries

indicators.note: the word lad turns round, read from its end

explanation.surface: The young man driving a delivery van becomes a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is a lout who wrecks property, a kind of thug.

clue.text: Climber riders sent sprawling

indicators.note: riders knocked flat land in a jumble, so the word's letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A plant or mountaineer knocks some horse riders over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Derris is a tropical climbing plant whose roots yield an insecticide.

clue.text: No longer a second helping for Oliver Twist

definitions.meaning: not continuing, ceased

definitions.text: a second helping for Oliver Twist
definitions.meaning: in Dickens the orphan asks for more gruel and is refused

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'no longer', and read literally it is the workhouse master's refusal of the orphan's famous plea for seconds.

clue.text: Go out of business. Say no more!

definitions.meaning: a shop that closes down for good is said to ... shop
a curt command to stop talking, be quiet

explanation.definitionFit: Closing a business for good and telling someone to be silent are both the same two-word phrasal verb.

clue.text: Computer print-out not easy to emulate

definitions.meaning: a paper version of data from a computer
read as difficult to imitate

explanation.definitionFit: A paper printout of a file has this name, and split into two words it says difficult to imitate.

clue.text: Deals with commercial malpractice

explanation.surface: Someone's dealings involve shady business practices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deals with' reads as handling a matter, but here it means buying and selling a commodity; 'commercial malpractice' looks like the definition and is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal in goods is to sell them as a business, so 'deals with' a commodity matches.

clue.text: Young chum has to have a game of chess and win it

parts.note: to play is to take part in a game
checkmate, shortened to mate, ends a chess game in victory

explanation.surface: A child's friend is expected to play chess and beat them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a child's friend to play with.

clue.text: Less than half those under 18 are in it

definitions.meaning: the smaller part of a group, below fifty per cent
a person below legal age is said to be in their nonage, a legal term for being underage

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the smaller share of a whole and the state of being legally underage.

clue.text: In time a renegade makes mistakes

indicators.note: the word for a renegade is set in the middle of the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a traitor or deserter

explanation.surface: Within some period, a turncoat commits blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is only a link word; 'In' sets the renegade inside the time, just after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed errors, especially printing errors corrected in a book.

clue.text: Anna and Iris originally were Persians

indicators.note: read as 'in an original way', a signal that the two names' letters are freshly arranged

explanation.surface: Two women named Anna and Iris were born in Persia.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ANNA and IRIS together are rearranged; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia is the old name for Iran, so its people are Persians.

clue.text: Call out for a single dairy product

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for single, as on forms or for a single bed
cream is a dairy product skimmed from milk

explanation.surface: Someone requests a single serving of something from the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call out for' reads like ordering; 'Call out' is the definition, a verb meaning shout, and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To scream is to shout or cry out loudly.

clue.text: Tidied up and left in a hurry

definitions.meaning: emptied of clutter
departed hastily, often taking everything

explanation.definitionFit: Emptying a room of clutter and bolting away in haste are both described by this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Mini snapshot should be carefully examined by contractors

definitions.text: should be carefully examined by contractors

parts.note: a print is a photograph developed from film

explanation.surface: A tiny photograph that builders ought to study closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Terms in tiny type at the bottom of a contract hide the conditions that anyone signing should read closely.

clue.text: Faint cry from a white supremacist

definitions.meaning: to lose consciousness briefly
read literally as a racist shout ordering black people out

explanation.definitionFit: Passing out is a common sense, and split into two words it reads as a bigot's exclusionary shout.

clue.text: So Arctic redevelopment is literally a puzzle

indicators.note: redeveloping something rebuilds it in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Building schemes in the polar region are said to be truly baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' means made of letters: this puzzle spells words with the first letters of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle or poem where initial letters of lines spell a word.

clue.text: How a pilotless plane flies to heavens above!

definitions.meaning: George is RAF slang for an aircraft's autopilot
an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise

explanation.definitionFit: A plane on autopilot is flown by 'George', airmen's slang, and the same phrase is a dated exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Unexpected opportunity to get a lot of fortuitous pots

definitions.meaning: a stroke of good fortune, a chance arising by luck
in snooker a break is a run of pots, here one made with flukes

explanation.definitionFit: A happy chance in life and a snooker run full of flukes share the same phrase; snooker is a cue game popular in Britain.

clue.text: An eight foot long snooker rest

definitions.meaning: an eight-legged creature, an arachnid
a raised rest used to bridge the cue over balls in snooker

explanation.definitionFit: An arachnid has eight legs, and a snooker player's raised cue rest shares its name; snooker is a cue game popular in Britain.

clue.text: A pie's made up of layers

indicators.note: made up of means composed, and here the letters are recomposed into a new order

parts.note: a tart is a pie, and 's here adds an S

explanation.surface: A pastry dish is built up in layers.
explanation.walkthrough: An indirect anagram: first swap 'pie' for TART, then rearrange A TARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers, especially of rock in geology.

clue.text: They dig out a suit

definitions.meaning: digging tools with flat blades
one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.definitionFit: Digging tools and one of the four card suits share the same name.

clue.text: One who strangles to obtain a necklace

definitions.meaning: a person who throttles someone
a close-fitting band of jewellery worn round the throat

explanation.definitionFit: A throttler and a tight neck ornament both take this name, one grips the throat and the other hugs it.

clue.text: Don't flag if you are the flag bearer

definitions.meaning: to flag is to tire; this urges someone to carry on with energy

definitions.text: if you are the flag bearer
definitions.meaning: a standard-bearer's job is literally to hold the banner aloft

explanation.definitionFit: An exhortation not to slacken also reads literally as telling a standard-bearer to hold the banner high.

clue.text: How's that for a public protest

definitions.meaning: in cricket the fielders' appeal to the umpire, shouted as a cry for a batsman to be given out
a loud general expression of disapproval

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket appeal is literally a cry of 'out', while the joined word means a loud general protest; cricket is a bat-and-ball game popular in Britain.

clue.text: First class workman turning up trumps apparently

definitions.meaning: a skilled, capable worker
a card player dealt plenty of trumps holds strong cards

explanation.definitionFit: A capable worker is a skilled hand, and a card player with strong cards in their grip holds a fine set.

clue.text: Watch your heart

definitions.meaning: slang for a timepiece, from its ticking
slang for the heart, which beats like a clock

explanation.definitionFit: Both a timepiece and the heart are slang names that come from their steady rhythmic beat.

clue.text: Reagan proposal as a Hollywood actor was about right

parts.note: a film star is a famous Hollywood actor

indicators.note: the word was is placed around the letter for right

explanation.surface: Ronald Reagan's idea, put forward when he was a famous film actor, turned out correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Reagan was himself a Hollywood actor, which makes the surface plausible; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: President Reagan's 1983 Strategic Defense Initiative, a space-based missile shield, was nicknamed after a film saga.
